concepts.name: AIF-C01 Exam Map
concepts.what: The exam is foundational and practical: choose the right AI/ML concept, AWS service, responsible AI control, or security/governance action for the scenario.
facts: 50 scored questions plus 15 unscored questions; no penalty for guessing.
Passing score is 700 on a 100-1000 scale.
Official domains: AI/ML fundamentals 20%, GenAI fundamentals 24%, FM applications 28%, Responsible AI 14%, Security/Governance 14%.
traps: Do not study advanced model math, coding, or infrastructure implementation as the main focus.
The exam rewards service/use-case matching and clear responsible-AI judgment.

concepts.name: AI, ML, And Learning Types
concepts.what: AI is the broad field; ML learns from data; deep learning uses neural networks; generative AI creates new content.
concepts.use: Questions asking which approach fits labels, unlabeled data, rewards, classification, or numeric prediction.
facts: Supervised learning uses labeled examples for classification or regression.
Unsupervised learning finds patterns such as clusters or anomalies in unlabeled data.
Reinforcement learning learns actions by reward feedback.
Classification predicts categories; regression predicts numbers.
traps: Do not use ML for deterministic arithmetic or simple rules.
Clustering is not classification because there are no predefined labels.

concepts.name: Generative AI And Foundation Models
concepts.what: Foundation models are large pretrained models that can be adapted through prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, or continued pre-training.
concepts.use: LLM, FM, modality, context window, token, embedding, or customization questions.
facts: Prompt engineering is the lowest-effort customization.
RAG adds external/private knowledge without retraining.
Fine-tuning changes behavior for a task using examples.
Continued pre-training adds domain knowledge from unlabeled data.
Pre-training from scratch is highest effort and highest responsibility.
traps: RAG is usually better than fine-tuning when facts change often.
Fine-tuning is not the cheapest first step for tone/format fixes.

concepts.name: Prompt Engineering
concepts.what: Prompts steer model behavior, output format, tone, language, constraints, examples, and reasoning style.
concepts.use: Questions about improving answers with least effort or controlling output style.
facts: Zero-shot = direct task with no examples.
Few-shot = give labeled examples.
Chain-of-thought = ask for step-by-step reasoning for complex tasks.
Role prompting = assign a persona.
Negative prompts tell image models what to exclude.
Lower temperature makes outputs more deterministic.
traps: Increasing temperature usually increases randomness, not accuracy.
Prompting is vulnerable to prompt injection, so use guardrails and validation for sensitive apps.

concepts.name: RAG And Vector Search
concepts.what: Retrieval Augmented Generation grounds responses in indexed documents by retrieving relevant chunks and passing them to an FM.
concepts.use: Private knowledge, changing FAQs, manuals, policies, enterprise search, vector database questions.
facts: Typical ingestion: extract content, chunk, embed, store in vector database, retrieve, generate.
Embeddings are numeric vectors that preserve semantic similarity.
OpenSearch Service can store/search vectors; Bedrock Knowledge Bases simplify RAG.
Offline batch work: create content embeddings and indexes. Online work: query embedding, retrieval, response generation.
traps: RAG does not retrain model weights.
Putting all documents into the prompt is expensive and hits context limits.

concepts.name: Amazon Bedrock
concepts.what: Amazon Bedrock is the managed AWS service for building and scaling generative AI apps with foundation models.
concepts.use: Questions about FMs, agents, knowledge bases, guardrails, model customization, on-demand/provisioned throughput.
facts: Knowledge Bases = managed RAG.
Agents = orchestrate multi-step tasks and tool/API calls.
Guardrails = safety filters, denied topics, word filters, and sensitive-information controls.
On-Demand = flexible pay-per-use; Provisioned Throughput = predictable steady/custom model capacity.
Custom model import and fine-tuning have more operational/security responsibility than simple prompting.
traps: Bedrock generates content; Comprehend analyzes text; Rekognition analyzes images/video.
Guardrails reduce unsafe output but do not replace IAM, logging, or data governance.

concepts.name: SageMaker AI
concepts.what: SageMaker AI is for building, training, tuning, deploying, monitoring, and governing ML models.
concepts.use: Questions about custom ML lifecycle, no-code ML, bias/explainability, labeling, model monitoring, feature reuse.
facts: Canvas = no-code ML.
Ground Truth = data labeling.
Feature Store = share/manage ML features.
Data Wrangler = prepare data.
Clarify = bias and explainability.
Model Monitor = drift/quality monitoring.
Model Cards = documentation and governance.
JumpStart = pretrained models and templates.
traps: Use Bedrock for managed foundation-model apps; use SageMaker for custom ML/model lifecycle.
Clarify explains and detects bias; CloudWatch monitors metrics/logs.

concepts.name: AWS AI Service Chooser
concepts.what: Many AIF questions are direct service matching.
concepts.use: When answer choices are AWS AI services.
facts: Comprehend = NLP, sentiment, entities, toxicity.
Rekognition = image/video labels, moderation, faces.
Textract = extract text/forms/tables from documents.
Transcribe = speech-to-text.
Polly = text-to-speech.
Translate = language translation.
Lex = conversational bots.
Personalize = recommendations.
Kendra = enterprise search.
Q Business = enterprise assistant over company data.
Q Developer = coding assistant.
HealthScribe = clinical speech-to-text and notes.
traps: Polly speaks; Transcribe listens.
Textract reads documents; Rekognition understands images/video.
Q Business is for employees querying business data, not image recognition.

concepts.name: Responsible AI
concepts.what: Responsible AI means fairness, explainability, privacy, security, safety, transparency, accountability, and human oversight.
concepts.use: Bias, transparency, hallucination, toxicity, inappropriate content, or regulated decision questions.
facts: Fairness = balanced representative data and bias testing.
Explainability = show factors/reasons behind outputs.
Transparency = document purpose, limits, data, and model behavior.
Privacy = protect sensitive data, minimize data, de-identify when appropriate.
Human-in-the-loop helps review high-risk outputs.
traps: Accuracy alone is not responsible AI.
A black-box model may be wrong when the question asks for explainability to stakeholders.

concepts.name: Security And Governance For AI
concepts.what: AI solutions still use normal AWS security: IAM least privilege, encryption, private networking, logging, monitoring, compliance evidence, and data governance.
concepts.use: Bedrock/SageMaker access, audit, encrypted S3, private API access, compliance reports, PII, and data residency.
facts: IAM controls who can invoke models and access data.
CloudTrail logs API calls.
CloudWatch monitors metrics/logs.
KMS manages encryption keys.
Macie discovers sensitive data in S3.
Artifact provides compliance reports.
Audit Manager helps collect audit evidence.
PrivateLink keeps supported service traffic off the public internet.
traps: Prompt instructions are not an access-control system.
Public S3 access is almost never the correct fix for AI data access.

concepts.name: Evaluation Metrics
concepts.what: Pick the metric from the problem type: classification, regression, generation, latency, cost, or business outcome.
concepts.use: Questions asking how to measure model quality or business impact.
facts: Accuracy = correct predictions / total.
Precision = among predicted positives, how many are truly positive.
Recall = among actual positives, how many were found.
F1 = balance of precision and recall; useful for imbalanced classes.
RMSE/MSE/R-squared = regression.
BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore = generated text similarity.
Latency/response time = real-time performance.
Conversion rate/cost per conversation = business impact.
traps: Accuracy can mislead on imbalanced datasets.
Business goals are not always measured by model metrics.

concepts.name: Inference And Deployment Choices
concepts.what: Inference means using a trained model on new data. Deployment choice depends on latency, payload size, traffic pattern, and cost.
concepts.use: Real-time, asynchronous, serverless, batch transform, large payload, sporadic traffic questions.
facts: Real-time endpoint = low latency interactive calls.
Asynchronous inference = large payloads or long processing.
Serverless inference = intermittent traffic without managing instances.
Batch transform = offline jobs over large datasets.
Provisioned Throughput = steady Bedrock traffic/custom model capacity.
traps: Batch is not for immediate user chat.
Serverless is not always cheapest for constant heavy traffic.

concepts.name: Data Preparation And Governance
concepts.what: Data quality, labeling, balance, retention, residency, and privacy controls affect model quality and compliance.
concepts.use: Bias, labeling, preprocessing, retention, data residency, PII, and feature sharing questions.
facts: Ground Truth/Plus = labeling and human review.
Data preprocessing cleans, filters, normalizes, and formats raw data.
Data augmentation can increase underrepresented examples.
Retention defines how long data is stored and when it is deleted.
Data residency keeps data in required regions/countries.
traps: More data is not enough if it is biased or low quality.
Do not move regulated data across regions when the prompt requires residency.

concepts.name: High-Yield Trap Pairs
concepts.what: These pairs explain many repeated dump questions.
facts: Bedrock vs SageMaker: GenAI FM app vs custom ML lifecycle.
Q Business vs Q Developer: employee business assistant vs coding assistant.
Comprehend vs Lex: analyze text vs build chatbot.
Kendra vs OpenSearch vector: enterprise search vs vector/k-NN storage/search.
Clarify vs Model Monitor: bias/explainability vs drift/production quality.
Artifact vs Audit Manager: download reports vs collect audit evidence.
traps: Do not confuse Transcribe and Translate.
Do not choose Rekognition for text documents; choose Textract.

questions.q: A company makes forecasts each quarter to decide how to optimize operations. An AI practitioner is writing a report to provide transparency and explainability to stakeholders. What should be included?
questions.explain: PDPs visualize the relationship between a feature and the target variable, making model decisions transparent and explainable to stakeholders.

questions.q: A law firm wants to build an AI application using LLMs to read legal documents and extract key points. Which solution meets this?
questions.explain: Summarization chatbots use LLMs to condense long documents (like legal texts) into key points efficiently.

questions.q: A company wants to classify human genes into 20 categories and needs to document how the inner mechanism affects the output. Which algorithm?
questions.explain: Decision trees are highly interpretable. Their tree-like structure makes it easy to document and explain the inner mechanisms affecting outputs.

questions.q: A company built an image classification model to predict plant diseases. Which metric should they use to measure correct classifications?
questions.explain: Accuracy is the standard metric for classification tasks, measuring the ratio of correct predictions to total predictions.

questions.q: A company uses a pre-trained LLM for product recommendations. Outputs need to be short and in a specific language. Solution?
questions.explain: Prompt engineering directly controls LLM output format, length, and language without changing model architecture or inference parameters.

questions.q: SageMaker production environment with 1GB inputs and up to 1 hour processing, needs near real-time latency. Inference option?
questions.explain: Asynchronous inference is designed for large payloads and long processing times (up to 1 hour) with near real-time callback support.

questions.q: Company wants to avoid creating new models from scratch. Adapt pre-trained models for new tasks. Strategy?
questions.explain: Transfer learning leverages pre-trained model weights and adapts them for new, related tasks, saving time and data.

questions.q: Generate images for protective eyewear with high accuracy and minimize risk of incorrect annotations. Solution?
questions.explain: Ground Truth Plus provides human-in-the-loop validation with high accuracy and built-in quality controls to minimize annotation errors.

questions.q: Bedrock FM needs to access encrypted S3 data (SSE-S3) but fails. Solution?
opts: Use prompt engineering to point to S3
questions.explain: The dump intends answer A: make sure the Bedrock service role can access the encrypted S3 data. For SSE-S3, S3 manages the keys, so the practical requirement is S3 read access through the role; if the scenario says SSE-KMS, the role also needs kms:Decrypt on the KMS key.

questions.q: Use language models for edge devices with lowest latency. Solution?
questions.explain: Small Language Models (SLMs) are optimized for low resource consumption and low latency, making them ideal for edge deployment.

questions.q: Use SageMaker for ML pipeline. Share and manage variables across multiple teams. Feature?
questions.explain: SageMaker Feature Store is specifically designed for centralized storage, sharing, and management of ML features across teams.

questions.q: Increase developer productivity using Amazon Q Developer. What can it do?
opts: Create code snippets, reference tracking, license tracking
questions.explain: Amazon Q Developer assists with code generation, referencing tracking, open-source license compliance, and security recommendations.

questions.q: Bedrock app in VPC, no internet traffic allowed for compliance. Service/feature?
questions.explain: AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between VPCs and AWS services without traversing the public internet.

questions.q: Educational game: 'Jar has 6 red, 4 green, 3 yellow. Probability of green?' Least overhead?
questions.explain: Deterministic mathematical probability problems are best solved with simple code/rules rather than complex ML models.

questions.q: Metric measuring runtime efficiency of operating AI models?
questions.explain: Average response time (latency) directly measures the runtime efficiency and user experience of operating AI models.

questions.q: Contact center app to gain insights from audio of customer calls. Solution?
questions.explain: Amazon Transcribe automatically converts speech-to-text, enabling further NLP analysis of call recordings.

questions.q: Petabytes of unlabeled customer data to classify into tiers for ads. Methodology?
questions.explain: Unsupervised learning (like clustering) finds patterns/groups in unlabeled data without predefined categories.

questions.q: Design a search app handling text and image queries. FM type?
questions.explain: Multi-modal embedding models map text and images into the same vector space, enabling semantic search across modalities.

questions.q: Fine-tune Bedrock FM for higher accuracy using company data. Strategy?
questions.explain: Fine-tuning requires labeled datasets where each entry contains an input prompt and the expected output completion.

questions.q: Check if IP is from a suspicious source. Solution?
questions.explain: Anomaly detection identifies unusual patterns or outliers (like suspicious IPs) without requiring labeled fraud data.

questions.q: OpenSearch Service feature for vector databases?
questions.explain: OpenSearch supports vector embeddings and provides k-NN (k-nearest neighbor) search for semantic similarity queries.

questions.q: Use case for generative AI models?
questions.explain: Image generation from text prompts is a classic generative AI application.

questions.q: Want to know how much info fits into one prompt. Consideration?
questions.explain: Context window defines the maximum number of tokens (input + output) a model can process at once.

questions.q: Chatbot needs to produce responses adhering to company tone. Solution?
questions.explain: Iterative prompt refinement is the standard way to guide tone, style, and format without retraining the model.

questions.q: Bedrock LLM for sentiment analysis (positive/negative). Strategy?
opts: Provide examples with labels then new text
questions.explain: Few-shot prompting provides examples of the desired task (input+label) to guide the LLM's classification behavior.

questions.q: Ensure only authorized users invoke Bedrock models. Identify unauthorized access attempts.
questions.explain: AWS CloudTrail logs all API calls, allowing security teams to audit and identify unauthorized model invocations.

questions.q: Host image classification model without managing infrastructure. Solution?
questions.explain: SageMaker Serverless Inference automatically provisions compute, scales to zero, and requires no infrastructure management.

questions.q: Receive email notifications when ISV compliance reports are available. Service?
questions.explain: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports and security agreements with notification support.

questions.q: Prevent LLM from being manipulated via prompt engineering to expose sensitive info.
questions.explain: Designing defensive prompts and using templates that instruct the model to recognize and reject injection attacks is effective.

questions.q: Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix: MOST customer ownership of security?
questions.explain: Building and training a model from scratch places maximum security and compliance responsibility on the customer.

questions.q: Automatically identify and categorize animals in photos without manual effort.
questions.explain: Object detection algorithms locate and classify multiple objects within images automatically.

questions.q: Limited budget, prefers flexibility without long-term commitment for Bedrock.
questions.explain: On-Demand pricing charges only for actual usage with no upfront commitments or reserved capacity.

questions.q: Quickly deploy and consume a foundation model within VPC.
questions.explain: SageMaker JumpStart provides pre-configured, ready-to-deploy FMs with VPC integration options.

questions.q: Secure LLM usage on Bedrock?
opts: Clear prompts + least privilege IAM roles
questions.explain: Security relies on strict IAM least-privilege access controls combined with well-designed, constrained prompts.

questions.q: Build SQL queries from employee input text with minimal tech experience.
questions.explain: GPT and other modern LLMs excel at text-to-SQL translation, allowing natural language to database query conversion.

questions.q: Deep learning model for object detection deployed. Process when analyzing a new image?
questions.explain: Inference is the phase where a trained model makes predictions on new, unseen data.

questions.q: Input data biased affecting image generation. Technique to solve?
questions.explain: Data augmentation balances underrepresented classes in training data, reducing bias in generated outputs.

questions.q: Supplement Bedrock Titan FM with relevant data from private sources.
questions.explain: Bedrock Knowledge Bases implement RAG, securely connecting FMs to private, up-to-date company data.

questions.q: Customize FM for diagnostics. Needs transparency for regulatory compliance.
questions.explain: SageMaker Clarify provides bias detection, model explainability (SHAP values), and fairness metrics required for compliance.

questions.q: Fine-tuned JumpStart chatbot must comply with regulatory frameworks. Choose two.
questions.explain: Compliance frameworks heavily emphasize threat detection mechanisms and strict data protection/privacy controls.

questions.q: Increase FM accuracy up to a specific acceptance level.
questions.explain: Increasing epochs allows the model to iterate over the dataset more times, learning finer patterns to reach target accuracy.

questions.q: Chatbot to decrease call center employee actions. Objective to evaluate effect?
questions.explain: Shorter call duration and fewer employee actions directly correlate with chatbot efficiency in handling queries.

questions.q: Functionality provided by SageMaker Clarify?
questions.explain: Clarify specializes in detecting data and model bias during training and post-training.

questions.q: Model performs well on training but poorly in production. Mitigation?
questions.explain: Increasing diverse training data helps the model generalize better and prevents overfitting to the training set.

questions.q: Determine customer sentiments from written reviews. Choose two.
questions.explain: Amazon Comprehend performs native NLP sentiment analysis. Bedrock LLMs can also be prompted for advanced sentiment extraction.

questions.q: Chat interface for PDF manuals. MOST cost-effective solution?
questions.explain: Knowledge Bases use RAG to retrieve only relevant chunks, saving tokens and avoiding fine-tuning costs.

questions.q: Evaluate LLM outputs for bias with LEAST admin effort.
questions.explain: Standardized benchmark datasets provide consistent, pre-labeled ground truth for automated bias/quality evaluation.

questions.q: Ensure generated content aligns with brand voice.
questions.explain: Well-crafted prompts with explicit tone, style, and brand guidelines steer LLM output without costly retraining.

questions.q: Loan discounts AI. Minimize bias. Choose two.
questions.explain: Proactively detecting data imbalances and evaluating/explaining model behavior to stakeholders are core responsible AI practices.

questions.q: Use custom trained model on Bedrock. Action required?
questions.explain: Custom models on Bedrock require Provisioned Throughput to ensure dedicated capacity and predictable performance.

questions.q: Identify Bedrock model matching employee response style preference.
questions.explain: Human evaluation using custom prompt datasets tailored to company preferences provides the most accurate style matching.

questions.q: Student copies GenAI to write essays. Challenge?
questions.explain: Submitting AI-generated text as original work without attribution constitutes plagiarism.

questions.q: Build LLM on company data. Concerned about environmental effect. EC2 type?
questions.explain: AWS Trainium (Trn) instances are purpose-built for training, offering superior performance per watt (lower carbon footprint).

questions.q: Interactive children's app generating stories. Ensure appropriate results/topics.
questions.explain: Guardrails for Bedrock provides configurable content filters and topic restrictions to ensure safe, age-appropriate outputs.

questions.q: Generate synthetic data based on existing data. Model type?
questions.explain: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are specifically designed to create realistic synthetic data mimicking real distributions.

questions.q: Predict hardware demand. No coding/ML experience. Analyze internal+external data.
questions.explain: SageMaker Canvas provides a visual, no-code interface for building ML models using internal and external datasets.

questions.q: Security camera flags specific ethnic group disproportionately. Bias type?
questions.explain: Sampling bias occurs when training data doesn't represent the real-world population, leading to skewed predictions for certain groups.

questions.q: Chatbot improves by learning from past interactions and resources.
questions.explain: Reinforcement learning uses reward signals (e.g., positive feedback) to iteratively improve decision-making strategies.

questions.q: Measure deep learning image classification performance. Metric?
questions.explain: A confusion matrix breaks down true/false positives/negatives, essential for evaluating multi-class classification models.

questions.q: Chatbot returns images. Ensure it doesn't return inappropriate images.
questions.explain: Moderation APIs scan outputs for NSFW/violent/inappropriate content before delivering to users.

questions.q: Store Bedrock model invocation logs to monitor input/output data.
questions.explain: Bedrock's native invocation logging feature directly captures request/response data to CloudWatch or S3.

questions.q: Inference on multi-GB datasets, no immediate prediction access needed. SageMaker option?
questions.explain: Batch transform processes large datasets asynchronously and outputs results to S3, ideal for offline analysis.

questions.q: Numerical representations of real-world objects for NLP/AI understanding.
questions.explain: Embeddings convert text/objects into dense numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning.

questions.q: Chatbot performs poorly on complex scientific terms. Improve?
questions.explain: Domain adaptation fine-tuning retrains the model on domain-specific data to improve understanding of specialized terminology.

questions.q: Bedrock sentiment analysis needs consistent responses to same input.
questions.explain: Lower temperature (near 0) makes LLM outputs deterministic and consistent, reducing variability.

questions.q: Teams access only their own customer data in S3 via Bedrock.
questions.explain: Dedicated IAM service roles for each team enforce strict data isolation and least-privilege access to specific S3 paths.

questions.q: Prevent Bedrock model from including patient PII in responses. Notify on violations.
questions.explain: Bedrock Guardrails filter PII/sensitive content in real-time. CloudWatch alarms trigger notifications on violations.

questions.q: Convert PDF resumes to plain text automatically.
questions.explain: Textract automatically extracts text and data from scanned documents, PDFs, and images.

questions.q: Change response style based on user age range with LEAST effort.
questions.explain: Adding a system instruction like 'Explain to a 10-year-old' directly in the prompt dynamically adjusts tone/complexity.

questions.q: Evaluate accuracy of FM for image classification?
questions.explain: Benchmark datasets provide standardized, labeled data to objectively measure classification accuracy.

questions.q: Automate document processing responsibly to avoid harm. Choose two.
questions.explain: Fairness metrics quantify bias. Mitigating bias in training data directly addresses root causes of harmful outputs.

questions.q: Creating correlation matrix, calculating stats, visualizing data. Pipeline stage?
questions.explain: EDA involves initial statistical analysis and visualization to understand data patterns before modeling.

questions.q: Suggest potential words to fill missing text in documents.
questions.explain: BERT uses masked language modeling to predict missing words based on bidirectional context.

questions.q: Automate generation of graphs showing total sales across locations.
questions.explain: Q in QuickSight uses natural language to generate business intelligence visualizations and dashboards.

questions.q: Bedrock LLM for intent detection using few-shot learning. Additional data needed?
questions.explain: Few-shot learning for intent classification requires labeled examples pairing user messages with their correct intents.

questions.q: Lower monthly cost for daily Bedrock invocation with 10 prompt examples.
questions.explain: Reducing prompt size decreases token consumption, directly lowering per-request costs.

questions.q: Marketing content sounds plausible but is incorrect. Problem?
questions.explain: Hallucination occurs when LLMs generate confident but factually incorrect or fabricated information.

questions.q: Prevent custom model from generating responses based on confidential training data.
questions.explain: Models can memorize training data. The only guaranteed fix is to remove confidential data and retrain from scratch.

questions.q: Evaluate translation accuracy of training manuals. Strategy?
questions.explain: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) measures the similarity between machine and human translations.

questions.q: Key benefit of Amazon Bedrock agents for retailer handling inquiries?
questions.explain: Agents automate complex, multi-step workflows by orchestrating actions across APIs and knowledge bases.

questions.q: Benefit of ongoing pre-training when fine-tuning FM?
questions.explain: Continuous pre-training on new data keeps the model's knowledge current, improving long-term performance.

questions.q: What are tokens in GenAI?
questions.explain: Tokens are the smallest units of text (words/subwords) that models process for input and generate as output.

questions.q: Factor driving inference costs on Bedrock?
questions.explain: Bedrock charges per input and output token. Optimizing prompt/response length directly controls costs.

questions.q: Manage data flow from S3 to SageMaker Studio notebooks.
questions.explain: VPC endpoints provide secure, low-latency private connectivity between SageMaker and S3 without internet traversal.

questions.q: Upload new dataset for Bedrock model validation.
questions.explain: Amazon S3 is the standard, scalable storage service for hosting datasets used by Bedrock training and validation jobs.

questions.q: Prompting attack that exposes configured LLM behavior?
questions.explain: Template extraction attacks manipulate the model to reveal its hidden system instructions or configured behavior.

questions.q: Company responsibility when using Bedrock?
questions.explain: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS secures the service; customers secure their data, IAM, and prompts.

questions.q: Compare toxicity of JumpStart models with LEAST operational overhead.
questions.explain: Bedrock's automatic model evaluation runs predefined toxicity/safety tests without manual setup.

questions.q: Testing security: get around safety features to generate harmful content.
questions.explain: Jailbreaking involves crafting prompts to bypass a model's ethical/safety constraints.

questions.q: Run SageMaker jobs in isolated environment without internet access.
questions.explain: Network Isolation restricts SageMaker containers from accessing external networks, ensuring data stays within AWS.

questions.q: Mechanism for ML team to audit custom models.
questions.explain: Model Cards standardize documentation of model purpose, training data, intended use, and limitations.

questions.q: Increase software development productivity using AI?
questions.explain: Code recommendation tools (like Q Developer) provide inline suggestions, debugging help, and best practices.

questions.q: Predict product demand using SageMaker DeepAR. Data type?
questions.explain: DeepAR is specifically designed for forecasting sequential time series data.

questions.q: Develop unbiased ML model for loan allocations?
questions.explain: Identifying and correcting class imbalance ensures the model learns patterns from all demographic groups fairly.

questions.q: Prompting technique to protect against prompt injection?
questions.explain: Adversarial prompting trains/models to recognize and neutralize malicious prompt injection attempts.

questions.q: Determine if fine-tuning enhanced LLM accuracy. Metric?
questions.explain: F1 score balances precision and recall, making it ideal for evaluating classification/chatbot accuracy.

questions.q: Increase specificity of RAG + Stable Diffusion product images.
questions.explain: Higher CFG scale forces the model to adhere more strictly to the prompt, reducing randomness and increasing detail accuracy.

questions.q: Chatbot for real-time contextual responses using company policies. MOST cost-effective?
questions.explain: RAG dynamically retrieves policy documents at runtime, avoiding expensive retraining/fine-tuning while ensuring accuracy.

questions.q: Use AWS Glue with minimal programming experience.
questions.explain: Q Developer can generate Glue ETL scripts from natural language descriptions, bridging skill gaps.

questions.q: Train image classification on diverse photos of insect bites from different demographics.
questions.explain: Ensuring training data represents all demographics mitigates bias, fulfilling the Fairness principle.

questions.q: Detect bias and explain loan approval predictions.
questions.explain: Clarify automatically detects bias and generates explainability reports (SHAP values) for model predictions.

questions.q: Metric for automatic model evaluation of text summarization on Bedrock?
questions.explain: BERTScore evaluates semantic similarity between generated and reference summaries using contextual embeddings.

questions.q: Predict flower classification based on petal/sepal measurements.
questions.explain: k-Nearest Neighbors classifies new data points based on the majority class of their closest labeled neighbors.

questions.q: Encrypt custom model artifacts with company-managed key.
questions.explain: AWS KMS manages encryption keys, allowing customers to use CMKs to encrypt Bedrock artifacts.

questions.q: Use LLMs to produce code from natural language comments.
questions.explain: Text generation capabilities allow LLMs to synthesize functional code from descriptive prompts.

questions.q: Assess if LLM makes text more coherent for language learners.
questions.explain: ROUGE measures overlap of n-grams between generated and reference text, evaluating coherence/quality.

questions.q: FM generates unrelated images. Modify prompt techniques.
questions.explain: Negative prompts explicitly tell the model what NOT to include, steering generation away from unwanted elements.

questions.q: Generate concise, feature-specific product descriptions.
questions.explain: Structured, category-specific prompts with explicit format/length constraints yield consistent, targeted outputs.

questions.q: Churn prediction model works on training data but fails on new data.
questions.explain: Higher regularization penalizes model complexity, preventing overfitting and improving generalization.

questions.q: Intelligent agents need DB supporting vector embeddings for similarity search.
questions.explain: Aurora PostgreSQL supports the pgvector extension for efficient storage and querying of vector embeddings.

questions.q: Factor relating to explainability of loan approval decisions?
questions.explain: Simpler, less complex models (like decision trees) are inherently more interpretable/explainable than deep neural networks.

questions.q: Analyze medication reviews and provide concise overviews.
questions.explain: LLMs excel at reading long text and generating concise, coherent summaries.

questions.q: Lead prioritization app: employees view/adjust variable weights.
questions.explain: Logistic regression provides explicit feature weights, allowing domain experts to interpret and adjust business rules.

questions.q: HOTSPOT: Select and order steps to develop well-architected ML workload. (See Cheatsheet for steps: 1. Define business goal, 2. Collect/prepare data, 3. Train/tune, 4. Evaluate, 5. Deploy/monitor)
opts: Business goal -> Data -> Train -> Evaluate -> Deploy
questions.explain: The standard ML lifecycle begins with business objectives, followed by data prep, training, evaluation, and deployment.

questions.q: Determine if FM effectively meets business objectives?
opts: Assess alignment with specific use cases
questions.explain: Model success is measured by how well it solves the specific business problem, not just technical metrics.

questions.q: Classify animal images with large labeled dataset, no new labeling.
questions.explain: Supervised learning uses labeled input-output pairs to train models for classification tasks.
